thread:
jonathan: FYI customer acme-inc seeing a burst of 5xx/timeouts starting ~08:20 UTC. Heavy p95 and tail timeouts from hosted endpoint, multiple support tickets incoming.

maya: Any correlation_id or example request we can forward to support? Is this across models or single model?

jonathan: One example request_id: abc123-def456. Gateway logs show repeated: "504 downstream timeout after queue wait 123456ms" and "503 queue_reject: depth_limit". It looks like request wait time in ingress queue exceeded 2 minutes before we dropped. Model: gptx-open-16k, seq_length ~8000 tokens (customer is sending long docs).

eli: Looking at live metrics for shard us-west-2-batcher-4 — queue_depth spiked to ~2.3k, continuous_batcher.pending_batches ~620, batcher_kv_spinups increased. We're hitting per-shard queue_depth_limit and fallback early_rejects didn't kick fast enough.

sre-bot: ALERT: ingress.queue_depth.hosted.us-west-2 >= 1800 (sustained 3m).

maya: Can you paste the minimal repro curl so support can reproduce locally? Also need the tenant header and example payload size.

jonathan: repro curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: acme-inc" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-open-16k","input":"<8k token document>", "max_tokens":4096}'
```

Notes: a stream of ~80 concurrent requests like this from a single tenant over ~30s reproduces queue pileup.

eli: Root cause hypothesis: long seq_length requests cause heavy KV cache state and longer service time per request. Continuous batching groups these into large batches so per-request latency balloons -> queue depth climbs -> early rejects are too late. Also per-tenant concurrency throttles aren't aligned with long-seq costs.

maya: Short-term mitigation options?

eli: 1) Apply per-tenant early_reject timeout policy (reject_at_queue_ms=60000) to drop obviously overdue requests. 2) Route acme-inc traffic to smaller model variant (gptx-open-4k) for now to reduce per-token cost/time. 3) Increase batcher worker count on the affected shard to drain backlog faster (can be done via autoscale override). 4) Add a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap (max_inflight=30).

jonathan: I've opened support escalation and recommended routing change + early_reject. Support team wants concrete runbook commands.

eli: Runbook steps I tested in staging:

1) Set early_reject policy: `redwoodctl routing set-policy --tenant acme-inc --policy early_reject_ms=60000`
2) Pin to fallback model: `redwoodctl routing set-tenant-model --tenant acme-inc --model gptx-open-4k --override 1h`
3) Increase batcher workers: `infractl scale batcher --shard us-west-2-batcher-4 --count +3`
4) Monitor: `metrics query "ingress.queue_depth{shard=\"us-west-2-batcher-4\"}"` and `alerts` for p95 and 5xx drops.

maya: Can you run the policy change and the model pin as a canary? We'll monitor customer impact and rollback if errors.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-policy-update for tenant=acme-inc by eli

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: routing-policy-update id=rp-2026-69321

jonathan: After policy + model-pin p95 dropped from ~18s -> ~2.4s and queue_depth back to ~200 within ~90s. Customer still saw some 503s during the peak but rate dropped significantly. :thumbsup:

eli: Next steps (medium term):
- Improve per-tenant cost-aware concurrency limits (consider seq_length heuristics).
- Add KV-cache prewarm hints for long-doc tenants to avoid spinups during bursts.
- Tune continuous_batcher grouping thresholds for long-sequence workloads (avoid creating huge batches that blow latency).
- Add automated canary that temporarily routes long-seq traffic to smaller variants when queue_depth > threshold.

maya: I'll update the incident ticket and support notes with repro curl, runbook steps, and mitigation timeline. We should also notify SRE/infra to look at autoscale thresholds for batchers.

jonathan: Thanks. Saving logs and adding full traces to the incident. If we see another spike we'll escalate to Dedicated trial for the tenant.

eli: copying ops-rotation to follow-up.

maya: closing loop with support now. Good job team.

sre-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: ingress.queue_depth.hosted.us-west-2 dropped below threshold.

jonathan: filed post-incident action items in #postmortems.
